dependencies.python: requires-python >=3.10; the classifiers list only 3.10, so CPython 3.14 is unverified (R2)
dependencies.litellm: Installed with the package although arm D never calls it. The pin already skips the compromised 1.82.7 and 1.82.8; the lock records the exact version and hash.
dependencies.extras: none: full, modal, dev and contree are not needed
dependencies.isolation: its own locked environment (uv, hashes recorded), never Optimus's .venv

static_findings.finding: The default model class sends a bash tool schema and requires native tool calls (models/litellm_model.py:64-71, models/utils/actions_toolcall.py:40-52). The Gateway's chat route returns message text only (src/optimus_gateway/chat_completions.py:48-65), so every turn would be a format error and the run would end RepeatedFormatError after three (agents/default.py:100-112).
static_findings.resolution: Use the candidate's own text-based action format: config/mini_textbased.yaml with actions_text.parse_regex_actions, exactly one mswea_bash_command block per turn (models/litellm_textbased_model.py:7-37). No replacement harness is needed.

static_findings.finding: The Gateway joins message texts without their roles (src/optimus_gateway/models.py:169-188) and the enforced route sends the provider one user message (src/optimus_gateway/model_policy.py, admit_request).
static_findings.resolution: The adapter writes each role into the text (tools/plan12_memory/harness.py, encode_transcript). The same single-message transport applies to all three models and is labelled in every arm-D result.

static_findings.finding: The LiteLLM model class prices each reply with LiteLLM from the provider's usage field and raises when it cannot (models/litellm_model.py:108-126). The Gateway reports gateway_usage and no usage field.
static_findings.resolution: The arm-D model class does not use LiteLLM. Cost comes only from Gateway receipts through parse_reply; the harness's own cost_limit is 0 (off) because it cannot price Gateway replies.

static_findings.finding: query() retries a failed call up to ten times with backoff (models/litellm_model.py:81-84, models/utils/retry.py:9-25). The Gateway already makes every safe resend, never re-sends a possibly billed attempt and marks each failure non-retryable (src/optimus_gateway/responses.py:150-160).
static_findings.resolution: The arm-D model class sends each request once. A non-200 reply ends the run with exit status GatewayError and keeps its receipts.

static_findings.finding: The local environment runs commands with shell=True, which is cmd.exe on Windows, and kills process groups only on POSIX (environments/local.py:72-92). The action format is bash.
static_findings.resolution: Run each case in the Docker environment with a bash interpreter (environments/docker.py:15-43) on a Linux container image pinned by digest.

static_findings.finding: get_model adds Anthropic cache-control markers by model name, and only LiteLLM model classes apply them (models/__init__.py:55-60, models/utils/cache_control.py).
static_findings.resolution: The arm-D model class sends no markers. Provider caching can still differ by model; cache tokens are recorded and stay null when unreported.

static_findings.finding: The harness saves the whole trajectory, including command output and raw replies (agents/default.py:159-190), so it holds repository source text.
static_findings.resolution: Trajectories stay in the run's own scratch under #248 custody. Evaluation artifacts keep only the ID-only trace contract (B1).

configuration.base_config: src/minisweagent/config/mini_textbased.yaml at the pinned commit; the overrides below are merged after it (run/mini.py:72-92)

agent.note: The base config's mode: confirm belongs to the interactive agent; DefaultAgent ignores it and asks nothing.

model.model_class: the arm-D model class (R1), given as a full import path
model.model_name: a run input: an exact registry model ID
model.templates: observation_template and format_error_template from the base config, unchanged

environment.image: a Linux image with bash, coreutils, grep, find and sed, pinned by digest at preflight (R3)
environment.workspace: the case snapshot at its cutoff, exported with git archive: no .git directory and no later history (R4)

transport.endpoint: POST /v1/chat/completions on an enforced Optimus Gateway (src/optimus_gateway/chat_completions.py)
transport.authentication: the Gateway's bearer shared secret only; no provider credential reaches the harness or Optimus
transport.request: harness.build_request: one user message holding the role-tagged transcript and a version-1 route_binding (registry hash, request id, output cap)
transport.admission: every request binds the approved registry snapshot; the model must be an exact registry ID eligible in it, and the route's approved reasoning level applies (src/optimus_model_policy/binding.py RouteBinding; src/optimus_gateway/model_policy.py admit_request)
transport.reply: harness.parse_reply: the text and finish_reason, and one receipt per attempt that may have reached a model; unbilled attempts carry no charge, uncertain ones stay unknown
transport.wait: the HTTP timeout is at least HOST_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (src/optimus_model_policy/binding.py:233), so a billed reply is never abandoned (R9)

reference_models.ids: run inputs: exact registry model IDs, recorded per run and never fixed in code
reference_models.parity: one registry snapshot, configuration, image and transport for all three

tools: one bash action per turn in the case container. No network, web, MCP, Optimus assembly, memory or Auto. Arm-D results are labelled with this tool set.

effort_and_stopping.effort: the registry route's approved reasoning level and the bound output cap; the harness sets no effort of its own
effort_and_stopping.stops: Submitted, LimitsExceeded (100 model calls), TimeExceeded (1800 s), RepeatedFormatError (3 in a row) or GatewayError
effort_and_stopping.pre_registration: These values join the other arms' rules before any run (case-review.json pre_registration). Changing them is a versioned revision of this record.

task_completion.equivalence: the same case query and the same answer schema as the other arms, graded by tools/plan12_memory/evaluate.py grade_trace
task_completion.completed: exit status Submitted: the first output line is COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT with return code 0 (environments/docker.py:140-150); the rest of the output is the answer
task_completion.not_completed: every other exit status counts as incomplete and is reported, never dropped or retried to green

adapter.scope: Requests are checked with the Gateway's real envelope validator, flattening and RouteBinding.from_wire. Replies are a labelled double built by the Gateway's own reply builders. This proves adapter behaviour only, never native transport or model compatibility.

runtime_obligations.point: The arm-D model class: it implements the pinned Model protocol (src/minisweagent/__init__.py), calls build_request and parse_reply, parses one action with parse_regex_actions, keeps receipts on a FormatError, sends each request once and ends the run on a non-200 reply.
runtime_obligations.acceptance_check: offline tests against the installed pinned package with a Gateway double, plus a revert check

runtime_obligations.point: Installation: a locked environment from the pinned commit on CPython 3.14, or a recorded older interpreter if 3.14 fails.
runtime_obligations.acceptance_check: a hash-locked install succeeds and minisweagent.__version__ is 2.4.6

runtime_obligations.point: Docker on the Windows host: Linux containers, the pinned image and --network=none.
runtime_obligations.acceptance_check: a trivial action returns code 0 and a network request from the container fails

runtime_obligations.point: No future leakage from the workspace.
runtime_obligations.acceptance_check: per case: no .git directory, the tree equals the cutoff commit's tree and the prompt names no withheld gold location

runtime_obligations.point: Gateway admission for all three reference models.
runtime_obligations.acceptance_check: each model is an exact eligible registry ID in the approved snapshot with its output cap inside the verified maximum; paid smoke calls only under the #248 budget

runtime_obligations.point: Each model keeps the text action format.
runtime_obligations.acceptance_check: the pilot reports the format-error rate per model; RepeatedFormatError counts as incomplete

runtime_obligations.point: Each model follows the role-tagged single-message transcript.
runtime_obligations.acceptance_check: a reviewed pilot sample shows no model treating its own earlier turns as user instructions; otherwise a versioned replacement decision

runtime_obligations.point: Receipts reconcile with the Gateway's records.
runtime_obligations.acceptance_check: every gateway_request_id in route_attempts appears in the Gateway usage log; the grader reports cost completeness

runtime_obligations.point: The wait covers the Gateway's own budget.
runtime_obligations.acceptance_check: the arm-D model class's HTTP timeout is read from HOST_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS

runtime_obligations.point: Trajectories stay out of evaluation artifacts (B1).
runtime_obligations.acceptance_check: output paths sit in the run's scratch; reports contain only ID-only trace records

replacement_rule: If any runtime obligation fails, a reviewer-approved replacement is chosen and versioned before benchmark execution. Evidence recorded here is not relabelled.
